title: Abelian inverse image preserves finite limits
statement: Let X and Y be schemes [def-pc-scheme] in a common universe and f:X→Y a scheme morphism. Put G = Opens.map f.base, the preimage functor from opens of Y to opens of X, and give both categories their open-cover Grothendieck topologies. Define L = G.sheafPullback AddCommGrpCat (Opens.grothendieckTopology Y) (Opens.grothendieckTopology X), the left adjoint to direct image on abelian sheaves. Then L preserves finite limits: it carries every limit cone of a finite diagram of abelian sheaves on Y to a limit cone of the image diagram on X. No flatness, separation, compactness, or nonemptiness assumption on the schemes or f is required.

proof.text: Specializes to G = Opens.map f.base, A = AddCommGrpCat, J = Opens.grothendieckTopology Y, K = Opens.grothendieckTopology X, after installing CategoryTheory.lan_preservesFiniteLimits_of_flat (E := AddCommGrpCat) G. The indexing category over an open U is nonempty (top is an object) and cofiltered (intersection is a common refinement; parallel arrows are unique), so G is representably flat. This hypothesis is synthesized by Mathlib. Abelian groups have limits and colimits; the forgetful functor preserves limits and filtered colimits and reflects limits, and abelian sheafification is left exact. The delivered two-line proof supplies the Lan instance and applies the cited sheaf pullback preservation instance.
